doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Improvising with birds, lawn mowers and children's sounds
summary: Jordan plays off ambient sounds, says he only wants to improvise whatever the label; Rowe mentions Parker and birds, and Jordan's kids recorded birds.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: They always was open though. And now I play with the birds in the morning, the birds and the trees. Well at school when the man, dealing with cutting the lawn, I play off of that and all the noises, and sometimes they used to move in the record players, you know how the make a lot of [wails] and I’d get to start playing with them and the people who had ears said man, listen to how he’s playing the sound of that. I said that’s right. And that’s where I’m at, man, now that’s really where my music is at. I mean sounds — you know and if they play the sounds I can play it and do something on it. Well that’s improvisation. That’s on the spot. And I got my ear to the point where I can do it, like the little children was in the gym, I told you, they started running around in sneakers and sliding and making sounds and I was playing it, and they could hear it. And I said that’s right, that’s where I’m at.

Now whether it’s jazz or not, I don’t know. I’ll let somebody else — I’m improvising. I don’t know if it’s jazz or not. But if jazz is supposed to be any improvising, all cultures you understand what I’m talking about? All I want to do is improvise, now if you call it jazz, good, you call it something else it’s still all right. I don’t have no problem with that.
Right. Let somebody else put the label on it.
That’s right, they have to, they have to. That’s right.
You know Buddy Colette told me that Charlie Parker got his nickname, his version of that story was that he used to play with birds in the morning in Kansas City.

That probably opened him up. And look, when Kent and them was little, they used to record the birds and bring them in, “Daddy listen to the birds.” They’d get up early in the morning and record the birds with a little tape recorder and bring it in for me. So you know how long ago that’s been. That’s something.
